mechanism: Senna as a stimulant laxative may increase gastrointestinal motility and reduce absorption of zoledronic acid if administered orally, though zoledronic acid is typically given intravenously; concurrent use may also increase gastrointestinal side effects including diarrhea and electrolyte disturbances.
action: Avoid concurrent use of senna as a laxative; if bowel management is necessary, prefer osmotic or stool softening agents; maintain adequate hydration and monitor electrolytes given zoledronic acid's effects on calcium and mineral metabolism.
